name: domainry-builder-v1
description: Build, evolve, repair, integrate, and verify a Domainry backend from accepted requirements or delivered frontend evidence. Use for metadata-first Domainry projects, frontend-to-Runtime replacement, Runtime integration, and full-stack defect routing. Keeps frontend evidence read-only except an explicitly authorized Data Exchange offline-export center.
---

# Domainry Builder V1

Each run owns one explicit Delivery Batch and follows exactly `requirements → model → apply → verify → done`. A batch is an initial Feature slice, Feature increment, cross-cutting evolution, or repair. Keep one project-visible TODO at `.domainry/development/<session-id>.md`; copy [the template](assets/DEVELOPMENT_TODO.template.md) only when it is absent, then resume its `Current stage`. Do not invent stages, state files, or continuation workflows.

The accepted product scope remains the baseline: never silently reduce it to an MVP. Put stable Requirement IDs and Feature keys in the current batch, record deferred Requirement IDs with planned Feature ownership, and include every shared resource or regression boundary affected by the batch. `done` means this batch is complete, not that deferred product scope was delivered.

Resolve this file's directory as `SKILL_ROOT` and set `DOMAINRY_CLI="$SKILL_ROOT/bin/domainry-cli"`. Use only that packaged CLI. The workflow has exactly five commands: `model capability`, `model plan`, `apply model`, `apply finalize`, and `verify`.

## requirements

Read [requirements and domain truth](references/requirements-and-domain-truth.md) and the [PRD template](assets/BACKEND_REQUIREMENTS_PRD.template.md). Settle domain truth inside this stage for the current batch and its dependency closure: actors and scope; objects, relations, states, defaults, and retention; commands, transactions, idempotency, calculations, and external effects; Reports and offline export intent; schedules, notifications, files, and integrations. Any required human approve/reject wait is a Runtime Workflow requirement, not two synchronous Handler branches. Any required downloadable Report export is a governed `report_export_controls` plus offline Data Exchange requirement, not a Report permission alone.

When frontend source exists, inspect it as evidence, including API Mock adapters, handlers, fixtures, seeds, and mutation side effects. `frontend/**` is read-only except for the authorized export-center slice described below. Treat it as evidence, not authority for missing policy. Record frontend defects for owner `frontend`; do not hide them with backend workarounds. Preserve the accepted product baseline in `docs/backend-requirements-prd.md` and record a traceable current-batch delta with stable Requirement IDs, sources, owners, acceptance results, Feature ownership and deferred scope. Do not advance while an unresolved choice changes current-batch observable behavior, authorization, money/units, an irreversible effect, or state flow.

## model

Select the one task profile and comma-separated requirement topics from the accepted current-batch dependency closure, then request one exact minimum reading plan. Read every returned `read_order` path once, in order, relative to `SKILL_ROOT`; do not independently scan the [capability index](references/capabilities/README.md) or template tree. The returned documents, including [backend model](references/backend-model.md) when selected, remain authoritative—the plan replaces manual discovery, not their semantics. Preserve the complete current desired state in `backend/model/*.json` and referenced `backend/reports/*.sql`; prefer one Feature per model file, and change only current-batch Features plus the declared shared-resource closure. Never edit `domain/**` or `.domainry/**`, and never emit compiler-owned `capability_assembly`, standalone Permission definitions, versions, ownership, or seed metadata. Author each ordinary Role directly as an array of exact `<permission_key>;<data_scope>` grants.

Classify every writable Object as either plain `direct_crud`, or `action_only` plus a source-owned Handler for any named, conditional, derived, state-changing, side-effecting, or cross-record command. Do not author new Automation. A human approval must be an enabled Workflow graph with an approval task, authorized assignee resolver, explicit approved and rejected branches, and terminal Action effects; standalone approve/reject Handlers are not the waiting process. Reports use `object_sql_v1`; every required export also authors the Blueprint `report_export_controls` closure (bounded rows, audit/download Objects and mappings, requester-owned grants, assurance/masking when required) while Runtime Report and Data Exchange own execution.

```sh
"$DOMAINRY_CLI" model capability --json --project "$PROJECT_ROOT" \
  --reading-profile <initial-delivery|feature-increment|handler-repair> \
  --topics <records,permissions,identity-profile,organization,reporting-line,workflow,scheduler,reports,report-export,notifications,connectors,agents,entrypoints,workspace-provisioning,files,domain-truth>
"$DOMAINRY_CLI" model capability --json --project "$PROJECT_ROOT" [--key <category>]
"$DOMAINRY_CLI" model plan --json --project "$PROJECT_ROOT"
```

`model plan` performs one immutable load of the complete current model, validates the whole cross-resource draft, derives capability and authorization closure, persists deterministic diagnostics/provenance, and reports the Ledger change set. On failure, repair the complete stdout `diagnostics` batch using each file/JSON Pointer, constraint, actual/allowed value and hint before rerunning; its `artifact` path, relative to `--project`, retains the full provenance. Never guess a capability key: use the index's exact keys; Runtime execution-only modules have none. A Delivery Batch is not a loader or apply filter. Confirm that every create, update and delete belongs to the batch or its declared impact closure; repair the named owner and rerun. Once valid, keep the model unchanged while reviewing removals and evolution-sensitive changes.

## apply

Read [project mutation](references/project-mutation.md), then apply the reviewed model:

```sh
"$DOMAINRY_CLI" apply model --json --project "$PROJECT_ROOT" \
  --go-module-path <domain-qualified-module>
```

Retain its immutable implementation packet. Read the compact packet index once: its `actions` array is the complete exact Action-context path list, `summary.shared_constraints` applies to every Action, and `summary.test_commands` is the copyable command contract for this delivery. Read its exact `verification.path` during apply—not after finalization—for the release-bound public Runtime route/auth/acceptance-fixture/evidence index and black-box example. Then read each compact Action context by exact path and follow that context's `read_order` once, in order, relative to `PROJECT_ROOT/backend`; those exact generated contracts and project-owned source/test files replace embedded source dumps and broad generated-tree scans. For this packet, implement only the project-owned backend source and paired tests, and create every required `backend/tests/businessflow` case for this batch. For a selected custom Connector, request its focused context with `model capability --connector-context <connector.provider>` immediately before implementation. Never edit generated source, manifests, receipts, caches, journals, or managed Runtime state.

The only frontend mutation exception is a Data Exchange offline-export center for an exportable Object SQL Report when `Frontend mutation scope: integration_authorized`; follow [its contract](references/frontend-offline-report-export.md). Otherwise report the owner gap.

Follow `summary.stage_boundary` literally: finish all project-owned source, then run `summary.test_commands.focused` and `summary.test_commands.business_flow_compile` before finalization; a full-tree failure caused by not-yet-generated composition is not an implementation failure. After both pre-finalize commands pass run `summary.test_commands.finalize`, then and only then run `summary.test_commands.full_tree`. These commands already contain the backend working directory, delivery build constraint, and project-local-plus-public hybrid `GOPROXY`; do not replace them with a default or local-only proxy. Once finalization succeeds, project-owned source is frozen for this verification attempt. Any later source change starts a new repair iteration and requires the focused/compile/finalize sequence again; do not continue the stale attempt into `verify`.

Finalize every delivered Handler and Connector:

```sh
"$DOMAINRY_CLI" apply finalize --json --project "$PROJECT_ROOT"
```

`apply finalize` enforces source call-site contracts, including guarded `ConditionalUpdate`; do not add manual grep gates. Run the affected backend test set before advancing.

## verify

Read [evidence levels](references/evidence-levels.md), [verification](references/verification.md), and [Runtime integration](references/backend-runtime.md). The implementation packet's verification guide and every required business-flow test must already have been consumed/completed during apply. Verify is read-and-run only: do not create, edit, rename, or delete project-owned source after finalization. Every current-batch business flow and affected regression boundary needs a complete project-owned case with explicit preconditions, ordered actions, and a terminal durable result; denial cases also prove unchanged state. For every module HTTP step, resolve the exact route in the implementation packet and grant that route's `authorization.permission` with its `required_role_grant.data_scope` to the selected actor Role before finalization; Report audience/source data access never substitutes for the executable route Permission. Decode Runtime record pages only as top-level `items`, with business fields in each `items[].data` and record metadata such as `id`/`updated_at` on the item envelope. Unchanged flows may reuse only current baseline evidence. Run the highest-risk changed case against the managed Runtime before broader flow verification.

```sh
"$DOMAINRY_CLI" verify --json --project "$PROJECT_ROOT" --address 127.0.0.1:<port>
```

`verify` reuses structural/package receipts only after their complete source, model, Runtime and dependency identities validate; otherwise it runs the complete backend tree and rebuilds. It always proves healthy start and same-cohort restart, then leaves Runtime stopped and emits stage/cache telemetry. `backend/tests/businessflow` is a black-box Runtime package: it may use published Runtime HTTP/client operations but never import project Handlers, generated capability/data fakes, or database drivers. For both phases every BF01-BF08 test emits its structured evidence marker exactly as verification documents. Treat Runtime identifiers and principal/context values as opaque. A shared login, health, read, or Action-catalog probe does not prove another named flow; each claimed Runtime case must execute its own ordered Runtime journey and read back its terminal durable result. Approval cases start the Workflow, observe the task, prove unauthorized denial, decide both branches, and read back process/task/business state. Export cases query and prepare the governed Report export, follow the requester-owned Data Exchange job to completion/download, and prove another actor is denied. Verify only requirement-observable denial, scope, conflict, rollback, replay, restart, worker, Report, export, file, notification, and provider behavior. Do not create a project evidence ledger or generic acceptance runner.

## done

Set `Current stage: done` only when every current-batch finding is resolved and current receipts, tests, durable observations, and Runtime identity support the claim. Report batch identity and scope, delivery identity, changed files, tests, Runtime result, highest evidence level, deferred Requirement IDs, and explicit limitations without claiming deferred product work is complete.

Project-owned edits are limited to requirements/TODO evidence, declarative model/SQL, backend source/tests, and the authorized export-center exception. Recoverable failures stay in the current stage: repair the responsible owner and rerun the same direct command.

# Requirements and domain truth

Use only for the `requirements` TODO section. Produce the accepted backend dependency PRD and freeze domain facts before capability discovery. Do not load model, apply, verification, or acceptance authority at this stage.

## Backend dependency PRD

Preserve the full accepted product demand as the requirements baseline. For a new project, complete replacement, or existing project increment, create or update `docs/backend-requirements-prd.md` from `assets/BACKEND_REQUIREMENTS_PRD.template.md`, or record an equivalent traceable current-batch delta that references the unchanged accepted baseline. Never silently reduce product demand to an MVP.

One Delivery Batch may implement an initial Feature slice, Feature increment, cross-cutting evolution, or repair. Record its stable Requirement IDs, planned Feature keys, baseline delivery/model identity, allowed shared-resource changes and affected regression boundary. Requirements outside the batch remain explicit deferred Requirement IDs with planned Feature ownership; `done` closes only the batch. A Feature slice must be dependency-closed: include any shared Role, entrypoint, Object, Action, Report, lifecycle or authorization change required for its behavior to be valid and verifiable.

Settle domain truth completely for the current batch and dependency closure before capability discovery. Deferred slices need enough stable identity and ownership to remain visible, but their unresolved details do not block this batch unless they change its observable result, authorization, amount/unit semantics, irreversible effect, or state flow. A later batch reuses the accepted baseline and resolves its own delta instead of rewriting unrelated requirements.

A source is structured when its rules live in stable titled/numbered sections citable as `<doc> §N`. If one section states a rule completely, cite it rather than restating it. A reference-mode PRD still carries requirement IDs, classifications, owner/capability mapping, decisions, acceptance criteria, and the matrices, each row citing its source section.

Read frontend evidence, when present, in this order: route/page registry and user journeys; typed application API; Mock adapters/handlers and fixtures/seeds; state stores and hooks; form/list/detail/report components; permission/menu guards; tests and stories; visible copy. Also read the current explicit requirement and latest accepted product/design documents. Requirements inspection is read-only. Mock or visible behavior proves demand or a current assumption, not a business rule without higher-precedence evidence.

When the frontend is already implemented, do not stop at API method names or TypeScript types. Search for every API dependency's Mock implementation, including request handlers, success/error responses, fixture collections, seeded identities, mutation side effects, generated identifiers, relation keys, enum/status values, timestamps, totals, and nested objects. Reconcile those concrete values with component reads and writes. Add any evidenced missing object, field, relation, lifecycle state, query shape, or representative worked example to the PRD, with its exact source path and an appropriate classification. Preserve conflicts and optionality: Mock-only fields remain `recommended` or `open` unless higher-precedence evidence confirms them, and decorative/test-only values do not become domain facts.

Use this precedence while preserving every conflict:

1. explicit current user decision;
2. latest accepted requirement or design contract;
3. latest implemented frontend behavior;
4. typed API and Mock semantics;
5. frontend tests;
6. legacy/reference implementation.

Classify every item as `confirmed`, `recommended`, `open`, `frontend_only`, or `legacy_reference`. Extract actors, journeys, observable success, objects, fields, relations, queries, commands, states, permissions/scopes, errors/conflicts, calculations, transactions/idempotency, external effects, and presentation-only behavior. Every write operation names authorization, observable validation/error behavior, transaction boundary, idempotency/retry policy, durable result, and acceptance proof.

Build one traceability row per in-scope requirement: `demand evidence → requirement ID → Feature key → Runtime owner/capability → model resource or approved source gap → permission/data scope → acceptance journey`. Account for every backend-bound typed API operation and route touched by the batch; reference the accepted baseline for unchanged rows and preserve explicit dispositions for deferred rows. Matrix cells are phrases; do not repeat table facts in prose.

## Critical ambiguity

Classify every unresolved choice before capability selection. Only `business_blocker` blocks model authoring, and only for the smallest affected slice.

| Decision class | Boundary | Handling | Blocks model? |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `business_blocker` | At least two concrete incompatible choices remain, and selecting one changes an explicitly required observable result, authorization allow/deny, amount/unit semantics, irreversible external effect, or business-state flow | Name the choices, affected requirements/model items, and obtain current user or accepted requirement authority | Yes, smallest slice only |
| `contract_discovery` | Runtime-owned formal code, canonical identity/context source, or accepted-fact-to-capability mapping | Defer discovery to the typed client/fixed capability contract; record a Foundation/Runtime gap if absent | No |
| `safe_implementation_decision` | Reversible technical choice preserving the accepted invariant | Defer to the published standard or record one conservative default and evolution path | No |
| `product_follow_up` | Product preference with a fallback that preserves required results | Record assumption, owner, fallback, excluded acceptance scope, and review trigger | No |

Security/privacy omissions default to least privilege, sensitive by default, and no export. An explicit broader-disclosure requirement remains a `business_blocker` until its authorization boundary is confirmed.

Use these nonblocking defaults without inventing product rules:

- Explicit exact decimals, comparisons, or sums do not require absent optional currency/unit/range metadata; block only a comparison/conversion slice where incompatible units change the required result.
- Explicit asynchronous approval may use an independent approval Object while the host remains unchanged until the terminal effect; missing edit/cancel/resubmit preferences are follow-ups.
- An explicitly immutable resource with no required business-role read needs no invented read actor; prove creation through a formal admin/seed path or persistence evidence.
- Weekday/morning intent with no timezone/holiday preference uses deterministic deployment timezone and standard weekday cron; block only explicit incompatible calendar outcomes.

## Domain truth design

Freeze domain facts before asking what Runtime can implement. When requirements contain calculations, historical facts, settlement, correction, or reversal, read [domain-truth-and-settlement.md](domain-truth-and-settlement.md) once and close its ownership, persistence, snapshot, trace, correction, and consumer decisions.

Financial, payroll, points, inventory-cost, and settlement facts remain reproducible after Settings change. If an event locks a result, define the write-side atomic action and immutable snapshot/ledger before its reports.

Before capability discovery, settle only the model-visible Report facts: the business question, Object SQL source of truth, parameters and defaults, result columns and meanings, authorization/audience, and whether export is required. Report query transport and export execution are Runtime-owned and stay out of the project model and PRD.

Every required Report export defaults to an offline Data Exchange job. When the project owns a frontend, the PRD also records the export-center route/audience and the actor-visible job-list/download outcome. If the active typed Runtime Client lacks the actor-owned Data Exchange export-job list, record a Data Exchange owner gap instead of inventing a route or browser-local list.

Verify the authorized Object SQL result, out-of-scope denial, offline job submission, actor-owned job-list visibility, and completed-file download when export is required. Do not turn Runtime execution internals into project acceptance cases.

Record any explicitly required current-database query-plan evidence and driver (`EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN`, `EXPLAIN FORMAT=JSON`, or `EXPLAIN (FORMAT JSON)`) as a business-flow verification obligation. Capability schemas are resolved during model routing; do not manufacture a separate platform gate catalog or case inventory.

## 1. Scope and evidence rules

- Backend scope:
- Managed Runtime database driver: `cohort_default` / `sqlite` / `mysql` / `postgres` (use an explicit driver only when the requirement authority fixes the later Runtime cohort)
- Verification database driver: `same_as_managed_runtime` (never require a second engine; every business-flow case and query-profile row must use the managed Runtime cohort's driver)
- Source document(s) and citation scheme (reference mode):
- Requirements evidence closure: non-empty this PRD + root `requirements.md` when present + non-derived `frontend/**` evidence when `frontend/src/**` exists; otherwise immutable external reference/snapshot recorded here
- Explicitly excluded frontend-only scope:
- Accepted baseline reused by this delta:
- Current-batch dependency closure:
- Deferred product scope preserved by this batch:
- Evidence precedence or approved exceptions:
- Known conflicts:
- Completed-frontend Mock inventory (API operation → handler/adapter → fixture/seed → PRD object/fields/relations/states; record `none found` only after searching):

Requirement classification values: `confirmed`, `recommended`, `open`, `frontend_only`, `legacy_reference`. Unresolved decisions separately use `business_blocker`, `contract_discovery`, `safe_implementation_decision`, or `product_follow_up` per `requirements-and-domain-truth.md#critical-ambiguity`; only `business_blocker` blocks model authoring.

## 2. Actors, roles, and journeys

| Journey ID | Actor / role | Entry route | Preconditions | Steps and backend interactions | Observable success | Failure / recovery | Classification | Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |

## 3. Routes and page dispositions

Every frontend route must map to one or more requirement IDs or be explicitly classified `frontend_only`.

| Route / page | Visible purpose | Backend-bound states and operations | Requirement IDs | Disposition | Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |

## 4. Domain objects and data contract

| Requirement ID | Object / concept identity | Fields and units | Relations / cardinality | Lifecycle states | Mock/fixture examples and provenance | Query, filter, sort, pagination | Sensitive data | Classification | Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |

## 5. Commands, state, and durable effects

Every write row must define authorization, observable validation/error behavior, transaction boundary, idempotency/retry, and durable outcome. Runtime-owned codes and reversible mechanism choices may cite their decision row rather than becoming product blockers.

| Requirement ID | Command / transition | Target and preconditions | Input / output | Authorization and scope | Transaction boundary | Idempotency / concurrency | Durable and external effects | Errors / conflicts | Classification | Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |

## 6. Calculations and policy versions

Distinguish occurred facts, summaries, and simulations before selecting any Runtime capability. Every material calculation row must close all business ownership and reproducibility columns. Exact decimal representation, an explicit comparison threshold, or summation remains modelable when currency, unit, or range metadata is absent: keep optional metadata nullable and enforce stated command preconditions. Only two or more incompatible unit/formula interpretations that change the explicitly required result block the smallest affected comparison/conversion or calculation slice. Runtime representations and reversible mechanics follow their nonblocking decision classes.

| Requirement ID | Fact type (`occurred` / `summary` / `simulation`) | Result | Inputs and units | Formula | Calculation Owner | Evaluation Time | Persisted Result | Policy/Rule Snapshot | Input Snapshot | Calculation Trace | Rounding point and mode | Correction/Reversal Strategy | Downstream Consumers | Report Source of Truth | Worked examples | Classification | Confirmation evidence |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |

## 7. Authorization, data scope, and navigation

An explicit update/delete denial can be modeled without a business read actor. When business-role read is not required, use formal admin/seed or persistence evidence for creation proof and do not invent business read permission merely to make acceptance convenient.

| Requirement ID | Role / actor | Permission | Record/data scope | Sensitive-field policy | Menu / route expectation | Allowed proof | Denied proof | Classification | Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |

## 8. Reports, Agent tasks, schedules, notifications, files, and integrations

An asynchronous approval with explicit approved/rejected outcomes may keep pending on an independent approval Object when the host lifecycle defines no pending state; the host remains unchanged until the terminal effect. Unspecified edit/cancel/resubmit behavior is nonblocking, with conservative no-expansion concurrency/idempotency that prevents duplicate effects. For an explicit weekday/morning schedule without timezone or holiday-calendar preference, use the platform/deployment-configured deterministic timezone and standard weekday cron and record the preference as a follow-up. Do not block unless an explicitly required multi-timezone or statutory-holiday distinction changes the demanded outcome.

### Object SQL Report and offline export contract

The project model exposes only Object SQL Reports. Record each Report's business purpose, SQL source of truth, parameters and defaults, result columns and meanings, authorization/audience, and whether export is required. Runtime owns Report query transport and export execution. Every required export defaults to an offline Data Exchange job; the owned frontend must provide one export-center list/download experience when frontend integration is authorized.

| Requirement ID | Capability | Owner / trigger / schedule | Inputs | Durable output / audit | Agent side-effect mode or Connector/external effect | Identity / allowlist / retry / reconciliation | Permission / scope | Classification | Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |

| Requirement ID / Report key | Business question / result meaning | SQL source of truth | Parameters / defaults | Result columns / types | Required permission / audience / data scope | Export required | Expected query result | Expected offline export result | Export-center route / audience | Data Exchange list/download support or owner gap | Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |

Verification proves the governed Object SQL result and authorization boundary. When export is required, it proves submission of an actor-owned Data Exchange job, visibility in the actor's export-center list, and completed-file download through the published Data Exchange operation. If the active Runtime Client lacks the actor-owned export-job list, record a Data Exchange owner gap rather than inventing a route or browser-local list.

## 9. Errors, empty/loading states, and recovery

| Requirement ID | Operation / page | Validation error | Permission / hidden scope | Conflict / concurrency | Transport / retry | Empty/loading behavior | Stable code or category | Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |

## 10. Runtime and metadata traceability

One row per backend-bound requirement. Account for every typed API operation as `platform_reused`, `metadata`, `approved_source_gap`, `frontend_only`, `superseded`, or `open`.

| Requirement ID | Frontend evidence | Runtime owner / capability | Fixed category / route | Model resource or source gap | Permission / scope | Business-flow ID | Disposition | Status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |

### Coverage totals

| Frontend routes | Routes dispositioned | Typed API operations | Operations traced | Write operations | Writes with auth + transaction + idempotency + error contract | Open critical rules |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |

## 11. Decisions and open questions

Use the four decision classes defined in `requirements-and-domain-truth.md#critical-ambiguity`. A `business_blocker` requires at least two concrete mutually incompatible choices and an exact affected slice where choosing changes an explicitly required observable result, authorization allow/deny result, amount/unit semantics, irreversible external effect, or business-state flow. Missing optional metadata, preferences, and mechanisms do not block settled core behavior. Runtime formal codes/identities/mappings are `contract_discovery`; reversible deterministic mechanics are `safe_implementation_decision`; nonblocking preferences with a complete fallback are `product_follow_up`. Security/privacy omissions default to least privilege, sensitive, and no export; an explicit demand to disclose a sensitive fact creates a `business_blocker` conflict.

| Decision ID | Affected requirements | Topic / conflict | Decision class | Observable business invariant | Assumption, discovered contract, or safe default | Decision owner | Confirmation / blocker or review trigger | Excluded verification scope / evolution path |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |

## 12. Business-flow verification contract

Each row is a confirmed PRD semantic execution contract, not a platform-generated case title. Runtime-owned identity/context values are resolved through their formal source and carried unchanged; every flow uses isolated setup so dependent cases cannot pass from residue. The implementer may add the minimum non-human contrasting identities needed for same-record allow/deny, Scope, and requester-isolation proof; fixture count does not assert product organization or role cardinality. The Agent turns these rows into ordinary project-owned tests during verify; the platform must not multiply them by Action, role, scope, or transaction dimensions.

| Journey / requirement | Actor | Formal Runtime identity / context source | Fresh seed / setup and dependencies | Exact route + executable Permission / scope | Command + actor-visible read surface | Positive oracle (target identity + non-empty facts) | Same-record scope contrast | Exact denied / conflict oracle + unchanged state | Durable effect / authoritative reconciliation | Restart / replay proof | Runtime/API evidence |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |

## Confirmation

- [ ] All routes are dispositioned.
- [ ] Every backend-bound typed API operation is traced.
- [ ] Every write operation defines authorization, transaction, idempotency/concurrency, errors, and durable effects.
- [ ] Every unresolved decision is classified; every `business_blocker` names at least two mutually incompatible choices, the explicitly required result/authorization/amount-unit/external-effect/state-flow difference, and only the smallest affected modeling slice; missing optional metadata/preferences/mechanisms do not block settled core behavior.
